name: NOT through the crossing
aliases: the binary black vertex is odd
summary: Moving a NOT (binary black vertex) through the crossing leaves a Pauli Z on the other wire.
description:
The *crossing* (fermionic swap) of the ZW-calculus is the map $|00\rangle\langle 00| + |01\rangle\langle 10| + |10\rangle\langle 01| - |11\rangle\langle 11|$: a swap that picks up a sign $-1$ when two $|1\rangle$'s (two fermions) are exchanged. It equals a SWAP followed by a CZ. It behaves like a symmetric braiding, except that it is only natural for *even* maps (those whose terms all have an even number of 1s); maps of odd parity, such as the black vertices, pick up signs. 

The binary black vertex of the ZW-calculus is the NOT gate (here the X-spider with phase $\pi$). It is *odd*, so the crossing is not natural for it: moving it through the crossing leaves the binary white vertex, the Pauli Z (Z-spider with phase $\pi$), on the other wire. Indeed, the crossing is $\mathrm{CZ}\circ\mathrm{SWAP}$ and $\mathrm{CZ}$ maps $X\otimes I$ to $X\otimes Z$.

In Hadzihasanovic's thesis ($ant_x^n$) and in Hadzihasanovic, Ng and Wang (2(g)) the Pauli Z is drawn as a [curl through the crossing](../fermionic-curl-minus-one/).
unchecked_reason: uses the fermionic crossing of the ZW-calculus, which is not a PyZX generator
